chunks: And as for what was narrated: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud from Salamah ibn Muhammad, who said: He informed us that Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Mahziyar from his father from his grandfather from Ayub ibn Nuh and others from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, who said: Abu al-Yas' informed me, saying:
A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — and I was listening — about the ritual bath (ghusl) when one visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), so he said: 'No.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a common title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: Ritual bath (ghusl), a major ablution required for ritual purity.
key_terms.قَبْرَ الْحُسَيْنِ: The grave of al-Husayn, referring to the shrine of the third Imam.

ai.seo_question: Is a ritual bath (ghusl) required when visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the ritual bath (*ghusl*) for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is not obligatory (*wajib*), distinguishing it from the *ghusl* required for major pilgrimage (*Hajj*) or Friday prayers. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that while visiting the Ahl al-Bayt is highly meritorious, it does not carry the same ritual purity requirements as the primary acts of worship, emphasizing accessibility for the devotee.
